title: Кофе со снотворным  (Coffee with Sleeping Drops)

segments.t: Back at Claude Monet, Louis delivers a cup of coffee spiked with sleeping drops to German's office, and Senya and Fedya sneak in as soon as the boss slumps over his desk.
Лезь давай к нему в карман.
Да я руку не могу достать.
Let's walk through each line of the office infiltration.
'German Mikhailovich, here is your coffee.' Returning to the coffee right here, Louis links the Russian words directly in the present with no word for "am", "is", or "are" needed.
'Just the way you like it.' Louis speaks wryly with a nod, watching Senya's face to see how the news lands.
'Why are you standing there, go on.' Senya speaks dryly right here and puts the weight on "stoish" ("stand", from "stoyat") as the exchange unfolds.
'And why does it have to be me right away?' Opening up evenly with Senya, Fedya puts the question word "pochemu" right at the start so Senya hears the focus immediately.
'Let's play rock, paper, scissors for it.' Addressing the paper with a nod, Fedya lets Senya see exactly where things stand.
'We already flipped a coin.' Mentioning a coin with Fedya, Senya puts the weight on "monetku" ("coin", from "monetka") as the exchange unfolds.
'Maybe we should play the cities game too?' Discussing the town before Senya, Fedya keeps normal statement word order here, turning the line into a question for Senya purely through rising pitch.
Лезь давай к нему в карман.
'Go on, reach into his pocket.' Senya proceeds pointedly with a smile, steering the talk right where he wants it.
'It is very funny to you, is it?' Fedya follows up smoothly in front of Senya and centers the remark on "smeshno" ("ridiculous") without any extra fuss.
'You had better help me instead.' Replying firmly to Louis, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 4 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'Well, what are you doing in here?' Louis questions bluntly what Fedya is actually getting at here.
Да я руку не могу достать.
'I cannot get my hand back out.' Mentioning his hand at once, Fedya brings in "ruku" ("hand", from "ruka") as the key Russian word here.
'I am afraid that he will wake up right now.' Addressing the right right here, the "-sya" ending on "prosnyotsya" ("right") marks an action that unfolds mutually or turns back on the speaker.
'He will not wake up, he is sleeping soundly.' Senya jumps in boldly watching Fedya, grounding the moment in plain reality. Now let's hear the whole scene again from start to finish.
Лезь давай к нему в карман.
Да я руку не могу достать.
Notice how Russian orders the hand game as 'rock, scissors, paper', and uses the indirect form when saying 'it is funny to you'. Until next time!
